subject: Hematology & ABG
title: CBC and Anemia Indices: A Practical Classification
preview: Combine hemoglobin, MCV, reticulocyte response and smear findings to classify anemia logically.

sections.title: Start with red-cell indices
points: Mean corpuscular volume describes average red-cell size; morphology and distribution may reveal mixed populations.
Ferritin is affected by inflammation, so its diagnostic interpretation is context-dependent.

sections.title: Use production-versus-loss logic
points: A low reticulocyte response despite anemia suggests insufficient marrow compensation.
An increased response suggests ongoing destruction, bleeding or recovery from treatment, depending on clinical context.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A single Mentzer-index cutoff is not definitive for thalassemia trait or iron deficiency.
Normal MCV does not exclude a mixed microcytic and macrocytic disorder.

quickRevision: Microcytosis commonly prompts assessment for iron deficiency, thalassemia and chronic inflammatory processes.
Macrocytosis can reflect B12/folate deficiency, liver disease, alcohol, hypothyroidism or reticulocytosis.
A reticulocyte response helps distinguish reduced red-cell production from blood loss or hemolysis.

quiz.question: Which red-cell index is used to classify microcytic versus macrocytic anemia?
quiz.explanation: Mean corpuscular volume (MCV). Mean corpuscular volume describes average red-cell size; morphology and distribution may reveal mixed populations.

valueSources.label: Adult MCV categories
valueSources.source: Merck Manual Professional — Evaluation of Anemia
valueSources.note: Microcytosis <80 fL and macrocytosis >100 fL are commonly used adult categories; laboratory and age context vary.
